body: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False here. `mp_context.Process` creates a `SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `BaseProcess` and not `multiprocessing.Process` (you can confirm with `isinstance(get_context('spawn').Process(...), multiprocessing.Process)`, which returns False). Before this PR, `kill()` was called unconditionally. Now a hung flusher (cause="hang") is never killed. A replacement process is spawned while the old one keeps running against the same shards, so two flushers produce the same segments concurrently (duplicate segments downstream), and every restart leaks another process. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or check `hasattr`/`not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

This has the same isinstance issue: a `SpawnProcess` is never an instance of `multiprocessing.Process`, so `terminate()` is never called on shutdown. Now that there are N processes, stuck flushers are left behind until the daemon teardown.

Once the deadline expires, `break` leaves the loop, so every remaining process skips the `terminate()` below. If the first process uses up the timeout, processes 2..N are never terminated. Instead of breaking, keep iterating (skip the wait but still terminate).

The default behaviour is inconsistent. The CLI defaults `--flusher-processes` to 1, but the factory/SpanFlusher default of `None` means one process per shard. `max_processes or ...` also turns an explicit `0` into "one per shard" without complaint, and a negative value makes `num_processes` negative, which later breaks the `i % self.num_processes` mapping. Validate the input (>=1) and pick one default.

Each process now gets its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`, and `flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max-flush-segments / len(assigned_shards))` from that buffer. With one shard per process, every process may flush the full `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` per cycle, so the total per-consumer flush volume, memory, and produce burst grow roughly N-fold. That silently changes what the option means. Split the budget across processes or document the change.

All per-process buffers use the same Redis client/cluster, so this runs `iter_cluster_memory_usage` (INFO on every node) N times on every `submit()` and counts each node N times. The ratio still comes out the same, but the Redis round-trips on the main thread multiply by the number of processes, which works against the goal of keeping the main thread minimal. One call is enough. The same applies to `record_stored_segments` above: it now issues N pipelines instead of one, which could be a single buffer over all shards.
`_create_process_for_shard` is never called. Remove this dead code.

This metric is tagged `shards`, but `produce`/`segment_size_bytes` use `shard`, and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with a single int value while these use a comma-joined list. Pick one tag key. Also note that a comma-joined shard list as a tag value can have high cardinality, depending on the configuration.

`if not process: continue` is dead code: `processes` only ever holds Process/Thread objects. In threading mode (`produce_to_pipe`), a "hang" restart can't kill the old thread, so it keeps flushing alongside the new one. That was already true before this PR, but now it happens once per shard group.
